title: The Open-Weight Schism
thesis: The frontier-AI debate has hardened from safety-versus-speed into a schism over who may hold model weights, and the EU's coming carve-out will encode one camp's worldview as the global default.
body:
For two years the fight over frontier AI was sold as safety versus speed. The real fault line runs elsewhere — over who is allowed to hold the weights [sy_3f6d1847c31e, sy_dbaa00b4db57]. As Washington tightens its export orders and Brussels drafts its exceptions, the major labs have hardened into camps that no longer share a definition of "responsible" [sy_d161e15367d3].

<define term="open-weight">a model whose trained parameters are published for anyone to download, run, and fine-tune offline, with no API in the loop</define>

<divide axis="Should frontier model weights be published at all?">
<camp label="Open by default">Publishing weights is the only credible form of external audit and a hedge against a handful of vendors owning the entire stack [sy_3f6d1847c31e]. [qt_8a9634dd25c1]</camp>
<camp label="API-only">A downloaded weight can never be recalled once misuse appears, so capability has to stay behind a metered endpoint that an export order can switch off [sy_dbaa00b4db57].</camp>
<camp label="Regulated middle">Neither absolute survives contact with the AI Act; gate only the largest training runs and leave the rest open [sy_d161e15367d3].</camp>
</divide>

This is not a clash of values. It is a clash over a single fact: whether a published weight is a telescope or a loaded gun [sy_3f6d1847c31e, sy_dbaa00b4db57].

<callout>The schism matters because whichever camp the EU's carve-out encodes becomes the global default — and the draft is being written right now [sy_d161e15367d3, pp_e27d7568051d]</callout>
